blind_spots.blind_spot: The payload has no path to an authorized configuration on the host vehicle it was validated against
blind_spots.operator_reality: EPADS only exists bolted to somebody else's UUV. Making it fieldable means an interface control agreement with the vehicle OEM, a re-validated buoyancy and hydrodynamic envelope for the modified vehicle, and an updated operating limitation set that the fleet's vehicle owner signs. A $1M SBIR does not compel the OEM to cooperate, and the WHOI licensing thread on the underlying transponder work adds a second IP owner to the same product. A payload company without host-platform authority stalls the moment the demo vehicle goes back to its owner.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Phase I and II both ran on borrowed REMUS 600 test time, where the vehicle's owner was a collaborator rather than a gatekeeper — the authority problem is invisible until transition.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: In-water tests were conducted with proprietary hydrodynamic A-Size dummy payloads carried on a REMUS 600 UUV.

blind_spots.blind_spot: Release is commanded over the least reliable link in the undersea domain, with no failure behavior described
blind_spots.operator_reality: Acoustic command underwater is tens of bits per second through multipath, thermoclines, and self-noise, with no delivery guarantee — the textbook denied/intermittent channel. The program office's next questions are the ones the abstract does not touch: what happens when the release command never arrives, when it arrives garbled, or when it arrives twice; is there a fail-safe or a timeout; and how does the operator ever confirm the payload actually deployed given the UUV is not surfacing to tell anyone. Deployment accuracy is quantified; command reliability and safing behavior are not mentioned at all.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: In a tank and in a controlled open-water test the acoustic path is short and clean, so the link never failed and never became a design driver.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Upon receiving an acoustic release command from the UUV, a motor opens a valve that floods a vacuum, making the payload negatively buoyant, and the payload detaches and descends to the seafloor target location.

blind_spots.blind_spot: No shipboard handling, safety, or load-out reality for a stored-energy pressure vessel
blind_spots.operator_reality: A 5 kg module whose actuation mechanism is a valve flooding an evacuated chamber is a pressure vessel with stored energy, carried aboard a ship and handled by sailors. Fielding requires a system safety hazard analysis, pressure-vessel certification for shipboard carriage, stowage and battery-handling approval, and a written load-out procedure a sailor can execute on a pitching deck in the dark with gloves on. Every one of those runs on a Navy timeline independent of the engineering, and none of them is scoped in a Phase II that ends at open-water accuracy testing.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The team's deep expertise is oceanographic research operations — a research vessel with a science party has none of these gates, so the procedure that works at WHOI has never been tested against a Navy safety authority.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: The approach uses a payload that can be neutrally ballasted in a range of seawater densities, including freshwater, so that it has no effect on host UUV buoyancy when attached.

opener_hook: ARMADA's Phase II abstract quantifies exactly the right things — two A-size payloads costing under 25% of REMUS 600 mission time and under 10% parasitic drag — and the last public milestone on armadamarinerobotics.com is still the June 2023 award; the question a program office asks after the tank test is what EPADS does when the acoustic release command never arrives.
what_they_do: Builds external payload deployment modules and modular propulsion for cylindrical unmanned underwater vehicles, letting a UUV carry and drop A-size payloads without changing its buoyancy.
